questions.question: The bioavailability of a drug given intravenously is:
questions.explanation: Oral drugs have lower bioavailability due to incomplete absorption and first-pass metabolism.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: First-pass metabolism refers to:

options.D: Metabolism of an orally absorbed drug in the liver before it reaches the systemic circulation

questions.explanation: Sublingual glyceryl trinitrate avoids first-pass effect.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: After how many half-lives is a drug given at a regular dosing interval considered to reach steady state?
questions.explanation: Steady-state concentration is reached after about 4–5 half-lives; elimination is also ~97% complete by then.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The therapeutic index of a drug is the ratio of:

options.A: Median lethal (or toxic) dose to median effective dose

questions.explanation: A narrow therapeutic index (digoxin, lithium, warfarin) requires monitoring.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A competitive antagonist:

options.B: Binds reversibly to the receptor, and its effect can be overcome by increasing the agonist concentration

questions.explanation: Atropine at muscarinic receptors is a competitive antagonist.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which route of administration gives the fastest onset of action?
questions.explanation: IV bypasses absorption; inhalation is also rapid.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Atropine blocks:
questions.explanation: Effects: tachycardia, dry mouth, mydriasis, urinary retention.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Neostigmine is used in the treatment of:
questions.explanation: It inhibits acetylcholinesterase, increasing acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In anaphylactic shock the drug of choice is:
questions.explanation: Acts on alpha, beta-1 and beta-2 receptors: vasoconstriction, bronchodilatation, increased cardiac output.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Propranolol is contraindicated in:
questions.explanation: Non-selective beta-blockade causes bronchoconstriction; also contraindicated in heart block.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Salbutamol relieves asthma by:

options.B: Stimulating beta-2 adrenergic receptors causing bronchodilatation

questions.explanation: Side effects: tremor, tachycardia, hypokalaemia.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Aspirin acts by:
questions.explanation: Low-dose aspirin inhibits platelet aggregation by blocking thromboxane A2 synthesis.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The most common adverse effect of NSAIDs is:
questions.explanation: COX-2 selective inhibitors have less GI toxicity but more cardiovascular risk.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The antidote for paracetamol overdose is:
questions.explanation: Replenishes glutathione; hepatotoxicity from NAPQI.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The antidote for opioid overdose is:
questions.explanation: Respiratory depression and pin-point pupils are the hallmarks.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A common troublesome side effect of ACE inhibitors such as enalapril is:
questions.explanation: Due to accumulation of bradykinin; ARBs do not cause cough.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Digoxin acts by inhibiting:
questions.explanation: Toxicity: nausea, visual disturbances (yellow vision), arrhythmias; hypokalaemia increases toxicity.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Furosemide acts on the:

options.C: Thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle (inhibits Na⁺-K⁺-2Cl⁻)

questions.explanation: May cause hypokalaemia and ototoxicity.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Warfarin acts by:

options.C: Inhibiting vitamin K–dependent clotting factor synthesis

questions.explanation: Heparin activates antithrombin III; monitor INR.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Glyceryl trinitrate relieves angina mainly by:

options.D: Venodilatation reducing preload and myocardial oxygen demand

questions.explanation: Release of nitric oxide; headache is a common side effect.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Penicillins act by:

options.A: Inhibiting protein synthesis at the 30S subunit

questions.explanation: Anaphylaxis is the most serious adverse effect.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Aminoglycosides such as gentamicin are associated with:
questions.explanation: Tetracyclines stain teeth; fluoroquinolones cause tendinopathy.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Peripheral neuropathy caused by isoniazid is prevented by supplementing:
questions.explanation: Isoniazid also causes hepatotoxicity.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Rifampicin causes:

options.D: Orange-red discolouration of urine and other body fluids

questions.explanation: It is a potent enzyme inducer.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Benzodiazepines act by:
questions.explanation: Flumazenil is the antagonist.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A characteristic adverse effect of long-term phenytoin is:
questions.explanation: Also hirsutism, ataxia, nystagmus and Dupuytren's contracture.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Carbidopa is combined with levodopa to:

options.D: Inhibit peripheral dopa decarboxylase, reducing peripheral side effects

questions.explanation: Allows lower doses of levodopa to be used.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The major adverse effect of insulin therapy is:
questions.explanation: Insulin shifts potassium into cells.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The first-line oral drug for type 2 diabetes is:
questions.explanation: Reduces hepatic glucose output; contraindicated in renal impairment due to lactic acidosis.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Long-term systemic corticosteroid use may cause:

options.C: Osteoporosis, myopathy, hyperglycaemia and adrenal suppression

questions.explanation: Never stop abruptly after prolonged use.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Baclofen reduces spasticity by acting as an agonist of:

options.D: GABA-B receptors in the spinal cord

questions.explanation: Abrupt withdrawal may cause seizures and rebound spasticity.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)
